tei:titleStmt.tei:title: בִּרְכַּת הָאִילָנוֹת
The Blessing of Flowering Fruit Trees in the Spring Season in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres

tei:div.tei:head: The Blessing of Flowering Fruit Trees in the Spring Season in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres

tei:lg.tei:l: To encourage a uniting of the blessed Holy One
with their Presence:
in awe and in love, in love and in awe,
to unite the names Yod-Heh with Vav-Heh
in inseparable unity
for the sake of all Yisrael.
And for the sake of all beings whose Life-Force, Soul, and Consciousness
is connected at the root to our Life-Force, Soul, and Consciousness
and connected to the Enclothing/manifestations of each of these, and everything closest to these
which are in the entirety of the Emanation-world, Creation-world, Formation-world and Action-world,
and which are from all pieces of Emanation, Creation, Formation and Action:
We declare ourselves ready and willing
to fulfill the commandment of the blessing
which was ordained by the sages of blessed memory
upon seeing fruit trees in bloom.
So may [the blessing] go up before you, Hashem our elo’ah and elo’ah of our ancestors,
as if we kept in mind all of the intentions deserved by this blessing and the secrets it holds,
and may this blessing be desired and accepted and welcomed before You
to identify and elevate, through it, all sparks of the holiness mingled throughout all vegetation,
and every Life-Force, Soul, and Consciousness which may be reincarnated in vegetation.
And you, El, through your abundant goodness and kindness,
light the way for them by the light of your face
to complete their clarification and correction.
Bless them, cleanse them,
your righteous kindness always grant them.
And may it be your Majesty’s desire, Hashem our elo’ah and elo’ah of our ancestors,
that through the merit we gain by incanting this blessing, this statement will be fulfilled through us:
“See, the scent of my son
is like the scent of the field that Hashem blessed.” (Genesis 27:27)
And may we receive abundance of ten blessings as written:
“And God will give you of the dew of the heaven
and of the fat of the land,
and much grain and wine.” (Genesis 27:28)
Peoples will serve you,
nations will bow before you,
you will have power over your brother,
and all your mother’s sons will bow to you,
may those who curse you be cursed,
and may those who bless you be blessed.” (Genesis 27:29)
May the words of my mouth and the flutterings of my heart be welcomed before You,
Hashem, my Rock and Redeemer. (Psalms 19:16)
And may the sweetness of Adonai our elo’ah be upon us,
and the works of our hands be established for us;
may they establish the work of our hands. (Psalms 90:17)

tei:div.tei:p:
Blessed are you,
YHVH (Hashem) our elo’ah,
cosmic majesty,
for there is nothing lacking in the world at all,
and created in it: good creatures
and pleasant trees
for the children of Adam to beautify themselves through them.

tei:l.tei:note: Some additional texts to learn about fruit trees from Tanakh, Midrash and Kabbalah:

tei:lg.tei:l: This one, your body, was like a palm tree, and your breasts clusters [of dates]. I said, I will climb up that palm tree, I will grab its branches. May your breasts be like clusters [of grapes] on the vine, the scent of your breathing like apples. And your mouth like good wine, going straight to my lover, lubricating sleepers’ lips. I am my lover’s, and his desire is upon me. (Song of Songs 7:8-11)

Rebbi Yishma’el said: The compassion of the Maqom is on the fruit of the tree....For if scripture cautions you [not to harm] the tree that makes fruit, all the more so the fruits themselves. (Sifrei Devarim §203)

Rebbi Abba taught: There is no greater revelation of redemption than that which the verse states (Ezekiel 36:8): “And you, mountains of Israel, you shall give forth your branches and you shall bear your fruit for my people Israel, for they shall soon come.” (Sanhedrin 98a)
When Rebbi Abba saw a tree whose fruit turned into a bird and flew away, he wept and said: If men only knew to what these things alluded, they would rend their garments! (Zohar 2:15b)

tei:note.tei:p: or “come true” through us. ‘Through’ us, not ‘for’ us — banu, not lanu.

This verse is crucial. Rei’aḥ connecting to ru’aḥ, and to the scent of flowers, and to being God’s child, and being a field that God has blessed. This is the verse that equates the soul of vegetation with the souls of us.

The ten blessings are as follows: 1. of the dew of heaven, 2. of the fat of the land, 3. much grain, 4. much wine, 5. people’s will serve you, 6. nations will bow before you, 7. you will have power over your brother, 8. all your mother’s sons will bow to you, 9. those who curse you be cursed, 10. those who bless you be blessed. Additionally, the verse that follows has ten words. The verse after it has sixteen, making twenty-six in total, and so we are blessed with ten blessings that are God’s unified name, Yud-Heh with Vav-Heh. And so we’ve come full circle!
In the Nusaḥ ha-Ari z”l, there is a slight variation in the wording: שֶׁלוֹ חִסַּר בָּעוֹלָמוֹ דָּבָר
Berakhot 43b. The variations for this blessings formulation are discussed here.
המקום, literally, the Place, a divine epithet.
